question: Four CPU-only de-risk verifications that can kill or clear the +25.6 ms/step width-3 FA2 lever (padded-B4) before any build, plus the dfwd rider.

headline.one_line: The plan survives, but ONE of its two load-bearing assumptions is FALSE and one is REPLACED BY SOMETHING BETTER. (1) The scope's hope that 'q and out are already slices of persistent buffers, so a zero-copy widen to [:128] may be available' is REFUTED at source: the b=3 FULL graph allocates query and output at exactly 96 rows per forward, so rows [96:128) do not exist and staging is MANDATORY -- measured cost 0.14-0.28 ms/step against a 25.59 ms/step gain. (2) The proposed shadow (seqused_k=64 + a pinned valid page) is strictly DOMINATED by seqused_k=0: at zero key rows the kernel takes an early exit that returns BEFORE the block table is ever formed and BEFORE Q is ever read, so the shadow reads NOTHING and writes deterministic zeros -- the NaN-poisoning risk and the pinned-page requirement both disappear.
headline.second_order: The wave model does NOT generalise to GDN -- but the reason it fails there is exactly the reason it holds for FA2, so the b<=2 zero-gain prediction survives for the FA2 launch specifically and for nothing else. The 0.3682 recovery fraction should be quoted as ~0.37 +/- 0.05, not to four figures.

verification_1_buffer_extents.question: In the b=3 FULL graph, what are the actual backing allocations for query/output passed to the FA2 call? Do rows [96:128) exist?
verification_1_buffer_extents.answer: EXACTLY-SIZED AT 96 ROWS. They are NOT slices of a 128-row persistent buffer. Rows [96:128) do not exist in either tensor; a zero-copy widen to [:128] is an out-of-bounds read of 393,216 B and an out-of-bounds WRITE of 393,216 B into the cudagraph's private memory pool. PADDING REQUIRES STAGING BUFFERS.
verification_1_buffer_extents.verdict: THE SCOPE'S ZERO-COPY HOPE IS REFUTED

chain_of_custody.claim: There are four separate FULL decode cudagraphs, one per width, and the width-3 graph runs at 96 tokens (not padded to 128).
chain_of_custody.source_evidence: vllm/config/vllm.py:1473-1487 -- max_cudagraph_capture_size = min(max_num_seqs * decode_query_len * 2, 512) = min(4*32*2, 512) = 256, then min(max_num_batched_tokens=8192, 256) = 256. vllm/config/compilation.py:1426-1471 adjust_cudagraph_sizes_for_spec_decode rounds every default capture size UP to a multiple of uniform_decode_query_len = 1 + num_speculative_tokens = 32. vllm/v1/cudagraph_dispatcher.py:206-230 then restricts the FULL decode keys to sizes <= uniform_decode_query_len * max_num_seqs = 128, leaving exactly [32, 64, 96, 128]. vllm/v1/cudagraph_dispatcher.py:140-155 _create_padded_batch_descriptor: num_tokens_padded = _bs_to_padded_graph_size[num_tokens] (96 -> 96, an exact capture size), num_reqs = num_tokens_padded // 32 = 3.
chain_of_custody.measured_corroboration: In the banked width-4 nsys sqlite, vllm::reshape_and_cache_flash_kernel (StringIds 219) inside fr13.fixed32.step but OUTSIDE fr13.fixed32.dfwd has gridX in {32, 64, 96, 128} with counts {64, 1184, 3792, 3600} = 16 target layers x {4, 74, 237, 225} steps. reshape_and_cache_flash's gridX is literally slot_mapping.size(0) = num_input_tokens (csrc/cache_kernels.cu). Width-3 steps run at 96 tokens. If they were padded into the 128-token graph the FA2 tree gridY would read 4; it reads 3 (grid (1,3,24), 3792 launches).

chain_of_custody.claim: query and output are allocated fresh per attention layer per forward at exactly num_input_tokens rows. Neither is a slice of anything larger.
chain_of_custody.source_evidence: vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py:493-508 -- 'num_tokens = query.shape[0]; output_shape = torch.Size((num_tokens, self.num_heads * self.head_size_v)); output = torch.empty(output_shape, ...); query = query.view(-1, self.num_heads, self.head_size); output = output.view(-1, self.num_heads, self.head_size_v)'. The producer of query is vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_next.py:279-302 (Qwen3NextAttention.forward): qkv_proj -> split -> q_norm(...) -> rotary_emb -> self.attn(q, k, v). q is the q_norm output, a fresh [T, 24*256] tensor. T = num_input_tokens = 96 in the width-3 graph.
chain_of_custody.implication: query is (96,24,256) bf16 contiguous (1,179,648 B), stride (6144,256,1). output is the same. Reading query rows [96:128) reads 393,216 B past the end of the allocation; writing output rows [96:128) writes 393,216 B past the end. Both allocations come from the cudagraph's private pool during capture (opaque_attention_op() is True on CUDA -- vllm/platforms/cuda.py:451 -- so the attention is an opaque custom op and the buffers are Inductor/allocator-managed and packed), so an OOB write silently corrupts a neighbouring tensor rather than faulting.

chain_of_custody.claim: The C++ side independently forces the padded out= to be 128 rows.
chain_of_custody.source_evidence: flash_api.cpp mha_varlen_fwd_impl: CHECK_SHAPE(q, total_q, num_heads, head_size) and CHECK_SHAPE(out, sizes[0], sizes[1], head_size) where sizes = q.sizes(). A 128-row q therefore REQUIRES a 128-row out; there is no way to pass a 128-row q with a 96-row out.

chain_of_custody.claim: The rest of the padded operand set CAN be widened cheaply, because those ARE slices of persistent buffers.
chain_of_custody.source_evidence: vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:2170-2172 -- query_start_loc = self.query_start_loc.gpu[:num_reqs_padded+1] and seq_lens = self.seq_lens[:num_reqs_padded] are slices of persistent CpuGpuBuffers sized max_num_reqs+1 and max_num_reqs. vllm/v1/worker/block_table.py:68-71, 203-205 -- self.block_table.gpu is a persistent (max_num_reqs, max_num_blocks_per_req) int32 tensor and get_device_tensor(n) returns [:n], so block_table.shape[1] is a run-constant. Only q and out have to be staged.
chain_of_custody.note: gpu_model_runner.py:1990-1993 additionally guarantees self.seq_lens[num_reqs:].fill_(0) on every step, so a zero-copy torch.as_strided widen of seqused_k to (4,) would already carry a zero shadow entry. That is an EXTERNAL invariant; the reviewable patch pins its own (4,) buffer instead and copies [0:3], which is fail-closed and costs 12 bytes.

cost_model_correction.scope_estimate: ~0.2-0.4 ms/step, '<1.6% overhead' -- offered as a fallback if the zero-copy widen were unavailable
cost_model_correction.measured_basis: 96 x 24 x 256 x 2 = 1,179,648 B per tensor. Per target layer: q-in copy (read+write) + out-back copy (read+write) = 4,718,592 B moved. 16 target layers = 75,497,472 B = 72 MiB per width-3 step.
cost_model_correction.wall: 0.28 ms/step at the banked measured 273 GB/s LPDDR5X (results/fr13_attack_ladder_analysis_20260808/README.md:14); 0.14 ms/step at the 546 GB/s the capture's TARGET_INFO_GPU reports. Take 0.14-0.28 ms/step.
cost_model_correction.graph_nodes: 4 extra copy nodes per layer (q, seqused_k, block_table, out) = 64 per step; the seqused_k and block_table copies can be hoisted to the first target layer only (the branch resolves at capture time), reducing this to 34.
cost_model_correction.staging_footprint: 2 x (128,24,256) bf16 = 3,145,728 B = 3.0 MiB total, shared across all 16 layers and both widths, plus a (4,K) int32 block table (~2 KB) and two tiny int32 vectors.
cost_model_correction.net: +25.59 ms/step gross - 0.14 to 0.28 ms/step staging - 0.023 ms/step shadow stores = +25.3 to +25.4 ms/step net. Overhead is 0.6-1.2% of the gain. The scope's economics survive.
cost_model_correction.cross_layer_reuse_is_safe: The 16 target layers run serially on one stream inside the FULL graph, so cudagraph capture records a linear dependency chain: stage-in -> FA2 -> copy-out -> next layer's stage-in. One shared pair of staging buffers is correct.

implementation_hazard_found.what: The staging buffers MUST be allocated before any capture, but the selector never reaches a non-capturing width-3 decode: outside capture it takes the 'outside_capture' bypass (patcher line ~6146-6152), and inside capture an allocation would come from the graph's PRIVATE POOL and its address would be invalid once another graph owns that memory.
implementation_hazard_found.consequence: A lazy allocate-on-first-use implementation is silently wrong. The reviewable patch fails closed (raises if asked to allocate while capturing) rather than allocating in the pool.
implementation_hazard_found.required_fix: Allocate the staging from an explicit pre-capture hook. The fr10 patch already owns the capture lifecycle (_FR13_FIXED32_CAPTURE_CONTEXT is set/cleared around capture in scripts/fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py:5138-5191, 5507); the allocation belongs immediately before that, keyed on (device, block_columns).

route_b_considered_and_rejected.idea: Delete 96 from the FULL decode capture sizes so width-3 steps dispatch into the existing 128-token graph. vLLM's own num_reqs padding would then supply everything for free: query/output at 128 rows, cu_seqlens_q of shape (5,), seqused_k of shape (4,) with seq_lens[3]=0 (gpu_model_runner.py:1993), block_table of shape (4,K) with row 3 = NULL_BLOCK_ID (gpu_model_runner.py:2138-2140), and descriptor.num_reqs == 4 so the existing selector engages with ZERO python changes.
route_b_considered_and_rejected.why_rejected: The whole step would then run at 128 tokens instead of 96 -- every GEMM, MoE, GDN scan and norm grows by 33%. The banked width-4 step wall is 411.26 ms against a ~362-369 ms width-3 step; the FA2 tree difference accounts for only 80.20 - 69.51 = 10.7 ms of that ~46 ms gap. Route B pays ~35 ms/step to save 25.6. STRICTLY DOMINATED.
route_b_considered_and_rejected.why_it_is_still_useful: It establishes vLLM's OWN padding convention as the reference for inertness -- seqused_k = 0, block_table row = NULL_BLOCK_ID = 0, query_start_loc entries repeated -- and it is that convention (seqused_k = 0) that verification 2 adopts in place of the scope's seqused_k = 64.

verification_2_shadow_request_kv_geometr.question: Does the shadow request satisfy every relevant clause of _fr13_fa2_qrow32_b4_geometry_mismatches and the C++ TORCH_CHECKs as written? Which clauses see the shadow? What is a safe pinned page? Is the shadow observationally inert?
verification_2_shadow_request_kv_geometr.answer: NO CLAUSE ANYWHERE SEES THE SHADOW. Neither the 33-clause C++ TORCH_CHECK nor the python geometry predicate dereferences a single seqused_k or block_table VALUE -- both inspect only pointers, dtypes, shapes and strides. The only code that can observe a malformed shadow is the kernel body. That is the fail-closed hazard, and it is why explicit shadow clauses are mandatory rather than optional.
verification_2_shadow_request_kv_geometr.verdict: CLEARED, AND HARDENED: use seqused_k[shadow] = 0, NOT 64

clauses_the_shadow_touches: params.b == 4 -- b is cu_seqlens_q.numel()-1; the padded cu_seqlens_q is (5,) so b = 4. SATISFIED by construction.
params.total_q == 128 -- total_q is q.size(0); the staged q is (128,24,256). SATISFIED.
params.seqlen_q == 32 and params.seqlen_q_rounded == 128 -- max_seqlen_q is passed as decode_meta.max_query_len = 32; round_multiple(32,128) = 128. SATISFIED, unchanged from b=4.
params.block_table != nullptr && params.block_table_batch_stride > 0 -- pointer and stride only. SATISFIED.

params.cu_seqlens_k != nullptr -- the python wrapper synthesises dummy_cu_seqlens_k = torch.empty_like(cu_seqlens_q), so it follows the padded (5,) shape automatically (vllm_flash_attn/flash_attn_interface.py:240, 259). SATISFIED.
params.q_head_stride == 256, o_head_stride == 256 -- the staged buffers are contiguous (128,24,256). SATISFIED.
num_splits == 0 && force_split_kernel -- unchanged; force_split_kernel = paged_KV = true at flash_api.cpp:845. SATISFIED.
cpp_33_clause_check_flash_api_cpp_250_30.clauses_that_would_catch_a_malformed_sha: NONE. There is no value-level check on seqused_k or block_table anywhere in the 33 conjuncts.
shape_checks_in_mha_varlen_fwd_impl_that: CHECK_SHAPE(block_table, batch_size, max_num_blocks_per_seq) -- so block_table MUST be widened to (4,K); a (3,K) table with b=4 raises. flash_api.cpp:720
CHECK_SHAPE(cu_seqlens_q, batch_size + 1) and CHECK_SHAPE(cu_seqlens_k, batch_size + 1) -- both (5,). flash_api.cpp:722-724
CHECK_SHAPE(out, sizes[0], sizes[1], head_size) -- out must be 128 rows. flash_api.cpp:739

five_b_dependent_clauses: query.shape == (128,24,256) -- SATISFIED by the staged buffer with NO change, on the padded route.
cu_seqlens_q.shape == (5,) -- SATISFIED by the padded vector with NO change.
seqused_k.shape == (4,) -- SATISFIED by the padded vector with NO change.
block_table.shape[0] == 4 -- SATISFIED by the padded table with NO change.

tree_bias.shape in ((32,32),(4,32,32)) -- ALREADY SATISFIED AT b=3 WITH NO CHANGE AT ALL: TreeAttentionMetadata.tree_attn_bias is a single 2-D (32,32) mask shared by every request (vllm/v1/attention/backends/tree_attn.py:171-179, 146, 214), and _fr13_fa2_qrow32_b4_candidate_tree_bias already does tree_bias.unsqueeze(0).expand(4,-1,-1) for the 2-D case (patcher 6024-6035). The mask is b-INDEPENDENT.
python_predicate_fr13_fa2_qrow32_b4_geom.consequence: On the PADDED route the five clauses need no b-parameterisation to admit the call -- the padded operands are canonical b=4 by construction. What they need is (a) b-parameterisation to validate the INBOUND width-3 operands before padding, and (b) a NEW predicate over the OUTBOUND padded operands, because that is the only place the shadow can be inspected at all. The reviewable patch does both.
python_predicate_fr13_fa2_qrow32_b4_geom.note: The scope's framing ('five b-dependent clauses become b-parameterised') is correct for the NATIVE C++ widening route, where b=3 shapes reach the .so. On the padded route it is the inbound half of the job.

kernel_body.what_reads_the_shadow: StaticPagedQueryBlockInfo ctor reads params.seqused_k[bidb] (flash_fwd_kernel.h:78). That is the ONLY read of shadow metadata that happens unconditionally.
kernel_body.early_exit: compute_attn_1rowblock_splitkv, flash_fwd_kernel.h:750-855. With num_splits=1: n_blocks_per_split = ceil_div(seqlen_k,64); n_block_min = 0; n_block_max = min(ceil_div(seqlen_k,64), n_blocks_per_split). At seqused_k = 0 both are 0, so 'if (n_block_min >= n_block_max)' at :759 fires. NOTE this branch is NOT guarded by (Is_causal || Is_local || !Is_even_MN) in the splitkv path, unlike the non-splitkv path at :249 -- it fires unconditionally.
kernel_body.what_the_early_exit_does: Builds gO from static_query_offset (rows [96:128), heads bidh and bidh+1, via the kHeadsPerCTA==2 layout at :769-803) and gLSE at softmax_lse_ptr + bidh*total_q + bidb*32 (:804-829); clears the register tile; copies zeros out with the M-bounds check disabled (kStaticQueryTile is true, :846); writes +INFINITY to the 32 LSE entries (:850-853); RETURNS at :854.
kernel_body.what_the_early_exit_never_touches: block_table is first FORMED at flash_fwd_kernel.h:862-875 and gQ at :898-919 -- both AFTER the return. So at seqused_k = 0 the shadow reads NO query rows, NO K page, NO V page, NO block table entry and NO tree_bias entry.
consequences: The scope's risk 'Stale Q rows 96:128 may contain NaN/Inf' is ELIMINATED, not mitigated: Q is never read for the shadow.
The scope's requirement 'block_table[3][0] must be a valid page index' is ELIMINATED: the block table row is never dereferenced.
The shadow's output is deterministic (exact zeros in O, +INF in LSE), not garbage.

recommended_shadow_vs_scope_shadow.scope_proposal: seqused_k[3] = 64 (one K block), block_table row 3 = a pinned valid page
recommended_shadow_vs_scope_shadow.recommendation: seqused_k[3] = 0, block_table row 3 = NULL_BLOCK_ID anyway (pinned, never read)
why_zero_dominates: Reads nothing, so no NaN/Inf exposure and no dependence on page contents.
Never dereferences the block table, so the pinned-page requirement becomes belt-and-braces rather than load-bearing.

Cheaper: the 12 shadow CTAs store 32,768 B each (32 rows x 2 heads x 256 x 2 B) = 393,216 B per launch = 23 us per step across 16 layers at 273 GB/s, then retire. At seqused_k=64 they would additionally stage a full 64-row K and V tile and run a masking step.
It is vLLM's OWN convention for cudagraph padding slots (gpu_model_runner.py:1993 seq_lens[num_reqs:].fill_(0)), so the design does not invent a new inertness contract.
recommended_shadow_vs_scope_shadow.wave_arithmetic_is_unchanged: grid is compile-time (3,4,4) = 48 CTAs = exactly one 48-CTA wave (flash_fwd_fr13_qrow32_gqa_pair_hdim256_bf16_sm80.cu:90-93). At width 3, 36 CTAs do real work and 12 retire immediately; with 1 CTA/SM each real CTA still owns its own SM, so the critical path equals a hypothetical native (3,3,4) launch. The padding is wall-neutral.

safe_pinned_page_source.why_it_is_always_allocated: vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py:173-177: 'self.null_block = self.free_block_queue.popleft(); self.null_block.is_null = True' -- block index 0 is popped out of the free queue at BlockPool construction and is never handed to a request. vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:1111 guarantees num_blocks >= 1 for exactly this reason. It is a real page inside the allocated kv_cache tensor, so naming it is always an in-bounds address.
safe_pinned_page_source.vllm_uses_it_for_the_same_purpose: vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:2138-2140 -- 'Fill unused block table entries with NULL_BLOCK_ID (null block) for CUDAGraph padding. Block 0 is reserved for padding.' blk_table_tensor[num_reqs:num_reqs_padded].fill_(NULL_BLOCK_ID).
safe_pinned_page_source.residual_caveat: Its CONTENTS are unspecified (padded tokens carry PAD_SLOT_ID = -1 and are skipped by reshape_and_cache, so the attention KV at page 0 is whatever the cache allocation left there). Irrelevant under the seqused_k=0 design because it is never read; under seqused_k=64 it would be read, and even NaN there would stay confined to the shadow's own rows because there is no cross-CTA reduction (Split=false, no combine launch).

downstream_consumer_trace.question: Does anything in the b=3 step read output rows [96:128)?
downstream_consumer_trace.argument_1_by_construction: On the staging design, FA2 writes rows [96:128) of a PRIVATE buffer that only the FR13 helper holds a reference to. The copy-back is output[:96].copy_(staged_out[:96]). Rows [96:128) of the staging buffer are dead on every path.
downstream_consumer_trace.argument_2_the_rows_do_not_exist_in_the_: The full consumer chain in the width-3 FULL graph is: (i) flash_attn_varlen_func writes out=output[:96] (patcher production_replacement, emitted into TreeAttentionImpl.forward); (ii) Attention.forward returns output.view(-1, hidden_size), a (96, 6144) view (vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py:549); (iii) Qwen3NextAttention.forward does attn_output = attn_output * gate with gate of shape (96,6144), then output[:], _ = self.o_proj(attn_output) (vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_next.py:302-308). Every tensor in the chain has exactly 96 rows. There is no row 96..127 anywhere for a consumer to read.
downstream_consumer_trace.lse: softmax_lse is allocated INSIDE the op as torch::empty({num_heads, total_q}) = (24,128) fp32 (flash_api.cpp:756) and the patched decode call discards the return value. The shadow's LSE entries are indices bidh*128 + 96..127; the real entries are bidh*128 + 0..95. No aliasing, no consumer.
downstream_consumer_trace.no_cross_cta_hazard: The candidate launches a plain kernel<<<grid,...>>> with cluster (1,1,1), Split=false and no combine launch (flash_fwd_fr13_qrow32_gqa_pair_hdim256_bf16_sm80.cu:90-102). Shadow CTAs exiting early cannot desynchronise anything because there is no grid-wide barrier and no reduction across bidb.

what_the_byte_gate_must_still_prove: output[0:96] and softmax_lse[:, 0:96] are byte-identical between a native-b3 stock replay and the padded-b4 candidate replay, on all 16 target layers, on the pinned evidence set.

The poisoned-shadow variant is now CHEAPER to state: fill the staging query rows [96:128) with NaN AND set staged block_table row 3 to a deliberately absurd page index. Under seqused_k=0 both are unread, so the byte result must be bit-identical to the clean-shadow run. That is a much sharper test than the scope's version, because it fails loudly if the early exit is ever not taken.
The staging copy-back must be shown to be captured INTO the width-3 graph (a graph-node count assertion at capture end), not executed eagerly.

verification_3_mtp_dfwd_geometry.question: Does the draft head's FA2 call geometry satisfy the sealed kernel's TORCH_CHECK set if handed a lower-triangular tagged mask? If any clause fails structurally, the rider dies free.
verification_3_mtp_dfwd_geometry.answer: NO CLAUSE FAILS STRUCTURALLY. All 49 conjuncts plus the interface precondition are SATISFIED (34) or SATISFIABLE-BY-PYTHON (15). The crux -- the MTP head's KV cache geometry -- is RESOLVED and is BIT-IDENTICAL to the 16 target layers, because the draft head shares their single full-attention KV cache group.
verification_3_mtp_dfwd_geometry.most_binding_constraint: params.b == 4 && params.total_q == 128 (reinforced by set_params_tree_bias's own tree_bias.size(0) == batch_size at flash_api.cpp:433). The dfwd b distribution over the 540 in-step draft passes is {4: 225, 3: 237, 2: 74, 1: 4} -- b=4 is native in only 41.7% of steps, so the rider needs the SAME padded-B4 staging the decode lever needs.

gdn_result.structural_finding: The deployed FR13 tree scan (_tree_gdn_path_kernel, src/lumo_flywheel_serving/fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:10021 def, :16350 launch) has grid (48, 16, {1,11}) with NO BATCH AXIS -- batch is expressed as 48b LAUNCHES per step per level, not as a larger grid. gdn_result.decisive_test: The GDN prefill chunk kernels sweep CTAs in exact steps of 48 at PROVABLY CONSTANT per-CTA work (grid=(NT, 48), one 64-token chunk per CTA -- fla/ops/chunk_scaled_dot_kkt.py:145). Within a single wave (144 CTAs at 3 CTA/SM) time rises 2.05x (chunk_scaled_dot_kkt, 48->144 CTAs), 2.85x (recompute_w_u), 2.08x (_causal_conv1d, 120->560 within its 576-CTA wave) and 1.49x (chunk_local_cumsum). The wave model predicts 1.00x.
gdn_result.sharpest_statistic: Marginal cost of +48 CTAs, split by whether it crosses a wave boundary: chunk_scaled_dot_kkt +11.0% within (n=13) vs +13.6% across (n=5); recompute_w_u +13.9% within (n=13) vs +15.5% across (n=5). Crossing a wave boundary is statistically indistinguishable from not crossing one. Linear-in-CTAs fits R^2 = 0.9962/0.9960/0.9977; linear-in-waves fits are WORSE (0.9891/0.9906/0.9951) despite waves being a coarsening of CTAs.

verification_4_gdn_wave_model_control.the_mechanism_that_reconciles_it: FA2 tree is the ONLY kernel in the capture pinned to exactly 1 CTA/SM. Every GDN kernel has occupancy 2-12 CTAs/SM, so its co-resident CTAs time-share issue slots and there is no free region past the first CTA per SM. The wave model is a property of THIS KERNEL'S 98,304 B shared-memory footprint against a 102,400 B per-SM limit, not of GB10 and not of the workload.

the_four_caveats_that_must_be_honoured: 1. STAGING IS MANDATORY, NOT OPTIONAL. The scope's zero-copy widen is refuted: the b=3 FULL graph allocates query and output at exactly 96 rows. 3. USE seqused_k[shadow] = 0, NOT 64. It is strictly safer (the kernel reads nothing and writes deterministic zeros), strictly cheaper, and it is vLLM's own padding convention. It also makes the poisoned-shadow byte gate sharper: poison BOTH the Q rows and the block-table row and require bit-identity.

4. THE 0.3682 RECOVERY FRACTION LOSES THREE SIGNIFICANT DIGITS. The wave model has a measured 10-15% in-family residual (b=3 vs b=4 at equal wave count). Carry 0.37 +/- 0.05, i.e. 25.6 +/- 3.5 ms/step gross. Even the pessimistic end clears the sealed four-pass MDE by 3-5x.
